dct_description_sm: The data was collected to study the pathways of water-soluble organic contaminants in the Arctic environment and their various compartments (i.e. sea water, brine, sea ice, snow, air) using HCH as a model contaminant. Because the Arctic is often viewed as a sink or final destination for contaminants, and there are high concerns for contamination among the human population in the North (via country foods like marine mammals, which make up part of their traditional/subsistence diet and are exposed to high concentrations of some contaminants), it is important to understand the pathways through which contaminants travel and their mechanisms of exposure to all marine animals.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Persistent organic pollutants (POPs)
dct_title_s: Alpha- and gamma- hexachlorocyclohexane (HCH) concentrations and alpha-HCH enantiomeric composition in the sea ice, snow, brine, sea water, air and biota samples from the Amundsen Gulf, Canadian High Arctic
